newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mostly firmer following G7.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mostly firmer following G7.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures firmed in early trading as traders continued to digest the outcome of the weekend Group of Seven meeting in Berlin.

The G7 in a short statement said that the major misalignments in exchange markets, noted in its April 1995 communique, have been corrected. The G7 reaffirmed its view that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility is undesirable.
Brokers and analysts said the statement was not strong enough to prompt a shift in prevailing sentiment that still views the dollar as a buy, based largely on fundamentals.

The meeting left the impression that the G7 are "unified in rhetoric but I don't think they are unified in any kind of apparent direct assault on the market," said Mike Malpede, currency analyst, Refco Inc in Chicago. "I think the function of the market is to test their (G7) resolve to stop the dollar's rise."
"To me, nothing fundamentally has changed at all," said a floor broker. "Europe and Japan are in deep trouble."
Two G7 officials noted that the group did not directly address the issue of intervention. U.K. chancellor Kenneth Clarke said G7 did not see need for an intervention accord.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the G7 did not discuss using intervention but that it would cooperate closely if necessary.
Traders said the market still would remain leery of whipping the dollar higher, given uncertainty about what levels might provoke intervention.
That could keep dollar-buyers hesitant as well and possibly result nearterm in the "bane for the trade - stability," Malpede said.
"We're off to a slow start," added the floor broker. "We're going to see a slow (dollar) grind up."

Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of Japanese finance ministry's international finance bureau, said that Monday's afternoon rate of around 122.50 yen reflects a G7 agreement on the need for currency market stability. Bundesbank's Tietmeyer called financial market reaction to G7 appropriate up until now, with the message apparently understood.

At 0845 CST/1445 GMT, March yen firmed $0.000005 to $0.008178, marks firmed $0.0002 to $0.6046, Swiss francs added $0.7027, sterling dipped $0.0006 to $1.6294, Can dollar lost $0.0013 to $0.7415, Aussie dollar fell $0.0038 to $0.7568, Mex peso rose $0.000125 to $0.126075.
